mechanism_narrative: A continued recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT raises weekday foot traffic near offices and stations, which lifts retail and recreation spending within four weeks. The signal is strongest when both series rise together, because commuting and in-person activity jointly rebuild routine shopping trips.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -39.6 to -30.4 while TRANSIT improved from -71.3 to -68.1 over the last 4 weeks
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC does not rise relative to the prior 28 days in weeks after WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both increase for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL intensity remains elevated while GROCERY_PHARM continues to improve, households substitute toward nearby convenience and discretionary shopping, pushing RETAIL_REC up within two weeks. This effect fails if residential stay-at-home time stops rising or if grocery access normalizes without any retail spillover.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays above +15 while GROCERY_PHARM rises by at least 2 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL remained positive at 16.6 and GROCERY_PHARM improved to -10.0 by t-0w
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC falls or stays flat over the next 14 days despite RESIDENTIAL remaining above +15 and GROCERY_PHARM improving week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp fall in TRANSIT below its already depressed level signals a new mobility restriction or demand shock that reduces access to shopping districts and lowers RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks. The claim fails if transit stabilizes or rebounds and retail still declines.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -72 after being above that level the prior week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT was -71.3, -71.9, -70.0, then -68.1 over the snapshot window
failure_condition: Reject if a TRANSIT break below -72 is not followed by a lower mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days versus the previous 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS mobility draws discretionary outings away from indoor retail and recreation, reducing RETAIL_REC over the following week. This is a short-horizon diversion effect and should appear only when parks mobility jumps quickly from a recent trough.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by more than 8 points week-on-week from a negative level
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -28.1 to -17.1 in the latest week
failure_condition: Reject if a week-on-week PARKS jump above 8 points is not followed by lower RETAIL_REC in the next 7 days.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM continues to recover while WORKPLACES remains deeply negative, households are shifting toward errand-based mobility rather than leisure shopping, which suppresses RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks. The mechanism fails once workplace mobility improves enough to restore broader weekday spending.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -16.4 to -10.0 while WORKPLACES stayed negative at -30.4
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days while GROCERY_PHARM keeps improving and WORKPLACES remains below -25.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility indicates more time spent outside the home, which converts directly into more shopping and recreation visits over the next four weeks. The effect should be gradual and persistent rather than immediate.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 19.3 to 16.6 across the snapshot window
failure_condition: Reject if a two-week drop in RESIDENTIAL is not followed by a higher average RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days than over the prior 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous improvement in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES marks reopening of commuting corridors, which raises retail and recreation mobility only after a one-week lag as workers resume discretionary trips near transit nodes. The mechanism is strongest when both series are moving up together from low levels.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both rise week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -71.3 to -68.1 and WORKPLACES improved from -39.6 to -30.4
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC does not improve within 7 days after simultaneous week-on-week gains in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS mobility remains elevated while GROCERY_PHARM and TRANSIT stay weak, outdoor leisure absorbs discretionary trips without generating retail visits, so RETAIL_REC stays below its recent average over the next four weeks. The claim fails if retail rebounds despite weak transit and grocery movement.
candidate_trigger: PARKS is above its prior two-week average while TRANSIT remains below -65
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved to -17.1 while TRANSIT stayed near -68.1 and GROCERY_PHARM remained negative
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds its previous 28-day mean despite elevated PARKS and weak TRANSIT.
